clue.text: Newly draw ship's flag, apart from centre

indicators.note: apart from means without, and the centre of the flag's name is its middle letter, which is dropped

parts.note: the Red Ensign is the flag flown by British merchant ships

explanation.surface: An instruction to redraw a ship's flag, leaving out the middle of it.
explanation.walkthrough: RED ENSIGN has nine letters; 'apart from centre' removes its middle letter, the N.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo the plan or drawing of something is to draw it newly, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: How devoted people regard king, appropriately

parts.note: R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king
aptly means appropriately

explanation.surface: Loyal subjects look at their king in a fitting manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted people gaze with rapt attention, so the adverb describes how they look at something.

clue.text: Get determination and ambition with infusion of energy

indicators.note: an infusion is something poured in, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: drive is determination and ambition
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Gaining drive and aspiration with a boost of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something from a source is to get it, as in getting pleasure from music.

clue.text: Daft asset ruined firm

indicators.note: ruined means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A silly investment has destroyed a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a business, but it is the adjective, steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady and unwavering, firm in purpose, is the adjective sense.

clue.text: Happy one has nothing invested in a case featuring violent opponents

parts.note: glad means happy
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: invested in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a case in court is a trial
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cheerful person puts no money into a lawsuit between violent enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside A TRIAL to give ATORIAL; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat between gladiators in the Roman arena featured armed fighters set against each other violently.

clue.text: Chant used by shaman, traditionally

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chant that shamans have used by tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeated sacred word or phrase intoned in meditation is a kind of chant.

clue.text: Addition to speech a Liberal Democrat inserted

indicators.note: inserted means the democrat is put inside the other letters

explanation.surface: A Lib Dem politician adds something to a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An improvised remark not in the script is an extra put into a speech.

clue.text: Cab running without a permit, ultimately the reason for protest in Boston

definitions.text: the reason for protest in Boston

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cab running goes around the rest

parts.note: a taxi is a cab

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of permit

parts.note: on means running, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: An unlicensed cab driver, the thing that finally provoked protest in Boston.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking but here has its old sense of outside; 'running' means switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxation without representation sparked the 1773 Boston Tea Party, the colonists' protest over a tea duty.

clue.text: Makes short work of a Poet Laureate

parts.note: Robert Bridges was Britain's Poet Laureate from 1913 to 1930

explanation.surface: A Poet Laureate dispatches something quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes short work of' looks like the idiom for quick defeat, but read literally it means shortens.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut down a text into a shorter version is literally to make the work short.

clue.text: Usually three, four, or five names wrong — hard cheese

parts.note: in golf, par for a hole is usually three, four or five strokes

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of the following word are put into a wrong order

explanation.surface: Getting names wrong is just bad luck, hard cheese, as Brits say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Usually three, four, or five' is golf's par for a hole; 'wrong' shuffles NAMES into MESAN. 'Hard cheese' is also British slang for bad luck, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese, so this is a plain example of the category.

clue.text: Get annoyed about team returning panacea

indicators.note: returning says the whole assembled run is read backwards
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to rile someone is to get them annoyed
a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross about their team's return, needing a cure-all.
explanation.walkthrough: RILE goes 'about' XI to give RIXILE, and 'returning' reverses all of that.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a supposed cure for all ills, which is what a panacea is.

clue.text: After frantic hour, go long way in the main road

indicators.note: in places the assembled letters inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: after places the long way behind the shuffled letters
frantic describes wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: far means a long way

explanation.surface: After a hectic hour, someone sets off on a long road trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic' gives OROUGH; 'in the main' looks like a phrase meaning mostly, but 'the' is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A public road or street, especially a main one carrying through traffic, is a thoroughfare.

clue.text: Numbers of Romans infuriated

parts.note: every letter here is a Roman numeral
VI is six in Roman numerals
D is five hundred in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Crowds of Romans were furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is spelt entirely in Roman numerals: LI (51), VI (6) and D (500).
explanation.definitionFit: Livid is everyday language for extremely angry, a direct synonym of furious.

clue.text: Swallowing hard, before long editor becomes occupied

indicators.note: swallowing means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: in a bit means soon, before long
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An editor who gulps something down and then becomes busy.
explanation.walkthrough: IN A BIT 'swallowing' H gives the first seven letters; 'becomes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A house that is lived in by people is occupied, so the two adjectives match.

clue.text: A bit of caning by teacher — brilliant idea

definitions.text: A bit of caning by teacher
definitions.meaning: read cryptically, a master's stroke is one stroke of the cane from a schoolmaster
a stroke of genius, an inspired move

explanation.surface: Corporal punishment by a teacher, presented as an inspired notion.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as master's stroke, the first reading is one blow from the old-style schoolmaster's cane.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstandingly clever move or plan is called this, a stroke of genius.

clue.text: With touch, primarily, in fact

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the initial letter of the word before is taken

parts.note: actually means in fact

explanation.surface: A remark that touch is, in fact, chiefly what matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'touch' does double duty, in the definition and as the source of T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactual means relating to the sense of feel, so the adverb means by means of feeling.

clue.text: To inspect bank can be more revealing

parts.note: to scan is to inspect
a bank of seats is a tier, a row

explanation.surface: Checking a bank's accounts can expose more than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is a link; scanty clothing shows more of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpier clothing covers less and so shows more skin.

clue.text: Have more importance than dated fashion, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: out means no longer fashionable, dated, and way means fashion or manner

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned clothes still matter more, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed something in significance or value is to surpass it in importance.

clue.text: Noble and monarch mixed drink that's a hit, in return

parts.note: a count is a nobleman
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
punch is a drink mixed from several ingredients

explanation.surface: An aristocrat and a queen share a cocktail that goes down well.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow delivered in response to an opponent's blow, as in boxing, is a hit given in return.

clue.text: Flan male had after fast's prematurely ended

indicators.note: after places the male pronoun behind the shortened word
cut short before its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: fast means quick
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man ate a flan once his fast had broken early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like going without food, but it means quick, cut to QUIC; 'had' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An open pastry case with a savoury egg filling is a type of flan.

clue.text: Like fish, sometimes, but never animal or bird

definitions.text: Like fish, sometimes, but never animal or bird

parts.words: Like fish, sometimes, but never animal or bird
parts.note: the word fish can mean more than one, whereas the words animal and bird always mean just one

explanation.surface: A puzzling classification of fish, not mammals or birds.
explanation.walkthrough: It is about grammar, not biology: fish can be a multiple form, animal and bird never.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatical number: a form referring to more than one is the opposite of singular.

clue.text: Dramatic announcement in all directions? Fancy!

parts.note: the four compass points N, E, W and S
flash means showy, fancy

explanation.surface: A startling public statement made everywhere at once, greeted with surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy!' looks like an exclamation of surprise, but it is the adjective, showy.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief urgent item of breaking news interrupting a broadcast is a sudden, dramatic announcement.

clue.text: Releases from confinement or stoppage, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver the word is spoken, giving a similar-sounding one

parts.note: a freeze is a stoppage, as in a pay freeze

explanation.surface: Letting prisoners out of jail or halting the process.
explanation.definitionFit: To let out of prison or captivity is to give someone liberty.

clue.text: Unexceptional learner attached to university in republic

indicators.note: attached to means the learner is joined on at the end
in places the university inside the republic

parts.note: USA, the United States, is a republic
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An ordinary student at an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside USA to give USUA, with L attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal and ordinary, not out of the way, is unexceptional.

clue.text: What I do with large collection of diamonds, say, in the same place

parts.note: at the bridge table, what I do is I bid

parts.words: with large collection of diamonds, say
parts.note: holding a long suit of diamonds: em is short for them

explanation.surface: Someone describing their bidding with a big diamond holding, perhaps at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as bridge talk, holding lots of diamonds means 'I bid 'em'.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin used in footnotes to refer back to the same source or passage, literally in the same place.

clue.text: Left on vehicle, run back for another form of transport

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle, a taxi

indicators.note: back says the word for run is read from right to left

parts.note: to race is to run

explanation.surface: Abandoned in a cab, someone runs back to find other transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A car hauled up a slope by a moving wire is a means of travel, distinct from the cab.

clue.text: Male held back by reckless use of old material

indicators.note: held, with by as a link, means the reversed pronoun is gripped inside the word for reckless

parts.note: rash means reckless

indicators.note: back says the pronoun is turned around

parts.note: he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man restrained because he carelessly used old supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held back' reads as restrained, but 'back' turns the pronoun round to EH and 'held' (with 'by' a link) grips it inside the word for reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Recycling old ideas or content with little change is a noun meaning a reuse of existing material.

clue.text: OK, or better than OK

definitions.meaning: a phrase of grudging agreement, all right then
in excellent health or done excellently, more than merely fine

explanation.surface: A rating scale running from acceptable to good.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as a reluctant assent and as an intensified form of fine.
